newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH INFLATION LOWEST IN EU IN JANUARY.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH INFLATION LOWEST IN EU IN JANUARY.

text.p: Finland's EU-harmonised consumer price inflation rate was the lowest in the European Union in January, Statistics Finland (SF) said on Friday.

"According to the European Union's new harmonised consumer price index, Finland's annual inflation rate in January was the EU's lowest at 0.9 percent. The inflation rate for the whole of the EU was 2.2 percent," SF said.

Eurostat, the European Commission's statistics office, published for the first time on Friday harmonised consumer price inflation figures for all 15 European Union countries. SF published this figure for Finland already on February 14.
In January, Sweden and Luxembourg had the second lowest inflation rates, at 1.3 percent, and Greece had the highest rate, at 6.6 percent, Eurostat said.
The EU-harmonised CPI was developed for assessment of EU countries' qualifications to join econoimic and monetary union.

To qualify for EMU, countries must achieve price stability, and average annual inflation should not exceed by more than 1.5 percentage points that of the three EU countries with the best performance in terms of price stability, SF said.

Finland would continue to publish its national CPI inflation data, which "is still the best measure of Finland's inflation," though the EU-harmonised CPI figures show smaller inflation differences between countries than national indices, SF said.
Calculated by the EU-harmonised method Finland's January inflation was 0.3 percentage points higher than by the national CPI method, SF said.
It said the EU-harmonised CPI did not include principal costs of owner-occupied housing, public services and several other smaller consumption items.
"The EU index covers 83 percent of the national consumer price index. The missing 17 percent explain the differences between the index figures," SF said.

Finland's national CPI measure is based on a basket of goods stemming from consumption patterns in 1990, whereas Finland's new EU-harmonised index includes new consumption goods such as mobile phones, SF said.
